newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA bunkers dip on crude losses, other ports gain.
newsitem.headline: ARA bunkers dip on crude losses, other ports gain.

text.p: ARA bunkers dipped on Friday, but prices in the rest of Europe mostly firmed despite an almost total lack of demand, dealers said.
"The buyers seem to think that the prices are going to come down," one dealer said.
Traders said weakening crude futures persuaded buyers that bunkers would be cheaper next week.
Rotterdam 380 cst was down about $1, trading mostly in the range $115/$116 fob, as barges initially weakened.
Demand in the entire ARA region was barely 10,000 tonnes dealers said.
Hamburg offers for fuel oil were about $3 a tonne higher to around $125 fob despite the very thin market.
"Suppliers seem just to be trying higher levels," one trader said.
Mediterranean bunkers were steady to $2 a tonne firmer.
Fujairah softened by about $1 as crude came off. Singapore had earlier remained unchanged.
